passage:
The cafeteria let students vote for one new lunch menu item. The choices were curry rice, tomato noodles, vegetable dumplings, and chicken soup.
Most students expected curry rice to win. It was popular and smelled good.
However, vegetable dumplings won by a small number of votes. Some students were shocked. Later, they learned that many students who did not usually speak loudly had voted for them.
The cafeteria added vegetable dumplings every Thursday. They became more popular after students tried them.
The vote taught everyone something. The loudest opinion is not always the majority. When people have a quiet way to choose, the result may surprise you.
